subject: Rating variance escalation map & transfer windows
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme People Ops <peopleops@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Flagging cross-team rating drift — proposed escalation map attached

Folks,

I ran a quick pass on the post-calibration exports and there is a ~22% variance in distribution between our infra and platform squads for the "meets expectations" vs "exceeds expectations" buckets (see attached variance-matrix-q4.csv). Some of the differences look driven by differing rubric interpretations on impact vs. scope, and a couple appear to be manager-level inflation on two small teams.

Because a handful of those skewed ratings affect compensation bands and downstream headcount decisions, I want to propose a short escalation map to close the loop before we finalize letters. Draft escalation-map-v1.pdf is attached and includes:
- Criteria for mandatory review (variance >15% OR >2\" high outliers\" in a band)
- Triage owners (people manager, L4 Director, HR partner)
- Transfer windows and freeze periods tied to comp runs

Requesting:
1) Marissa — can you take point on the infra/platform split and pull the manager-level notes for the 6 affected reports?
2) Rishi — confirm whether HR is comfortable with the proposed three-day review window or if we need a formal exception process.
3) Lauren — please check whether this intersects with any open headcount transfers (I linked transfer-windows-calendar.ics).

I copied Acme People Ops because a couple of affected folks are on loan from them; we may need their input if re-banding or re-assigning is considered.

I'll schedule a short huddle at 3pm PT if that's helpful — otherwise reply with availability and I'll adjust.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of People Operations (EMEA & Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: variance-matrix-q4.csv (csv), escalation-map-v1.pdf (pdf), transfer-windows-calendar.ics (calendar)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Flagging cross-team rating drift — proposed escalation map attached

Olga — thanks for the heads up. I pulled the infra/platform breakdown and the variance appears concentrated in two small pods that ship as part of Platform Core. I attached a quick excerpt to the drive link (private) — will surface manager notes there.

A couple quick clarifications:
- The two managers flagged were late to submit calibration evidence; one tried to retro-fit project impact without peer corroboration.
- One of the reports was already under an informal performance plan; their case is borderline and may be sensitive if we roll back a rating.

I can own the manager note collection and draft talking points for a review with the Director. If we go the review route I recommend we:
- Use the variance >15% rule you suggested, but escalate to Director-level only for disputed cases that change pay bands.
- Keep all manager notes redacted when shared externally with Acme.

I can join the 3pm PT huddle.

—Marissa
Director, Talent & Org Effectiveness
Redwood Inference

Thanks for surfacing this, Olga. HR view: the three-day review window is tight but doable for cases that only require manager/Director reconciliation. Anything that touches compensation adjustments or transfers that affect payroll needs a minimum seven-business-day notice to complete audit and payroll checks (per our comp operations SLA).

Proposed small edits to the escalation map (I noted them directly in escalation-map-v1.pdf in the drive):
- Add a \"comp impact\" flag that forces seven-business-day process when set.
- Define who signs off on band changes (Director + HR partner + Finance rep). We should list the alternate approver when a signer is on leave.
- Add an anonymized evidence pack template for external vendor review (Acme).

Acme — if you see any blockers to providing redacted manager corroboration within a week, please flag now. Jane, looping you for context.

Rishi
VP, People Operations (Comp & Policy)
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick summary and action items after today's pass:

Summary:
- Root cause: mixed rubric interpretation + two manager submissions lacking peer corroboration.
- Scope: 6 impacted contributors across infra/platform; 2 of those are on informal plans.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Marissa: collect manager notes + redact sensitive content, upload to drive by EOD 2026-10-12. (Owner: marissa_cole)
- Rishi: confirm comp-impact flag and finalize sign-off chain; provide written exception path by 2026-10-14. (Owner: rishi_malhotra)
- Lauren: confirm transfer windows and block any movements that intersect with comp freeze; reply with calendar constraints by 2026-10-13. (Owner: lauren_bishop)
- Olga: schedule canary reviews for disputed cases on 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16; invite Director+HR panel.

Notes on external sharing: Acme People Ops — we will only send anonymized evidence packs unless there is explicit consent from the individual. If Acme needs a different format, ping Rishi and we'll adapt.

I'll update the escalation-map after Rishi's edits and publish v1.1 to the linked drive folder. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Olga
Head of People Operations (EMEA & Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
